messages:
Maria (CEO): thanks for coming to today's all-hands. leaving a sticky thread for quick follow-ups on the company mission and how to talk about competitors externally. please drop short notes.
Ajay (CTO): tech framing: lead with predictable production behavior (SLOs, rollouts, KV caching). competitors trade one of cost/simplicity/reliability; we bridge them.
Lena (Head Product): product phrasing idea: "Inference you can operate." short, action-oriented, implies ops controls + runtime. open to other one-liners.
Tom (Sales): field perspective: customers ask two quick Qs upfront: can you meet our SLA, and how hard is it to integrate? cost comes after. recommend sales docs that answer SLA+integration in the first page.
Priya (Eng): operational request: marketing collateral should always link to a tech appendix with test configs behind any performance claim. ops-bot: weekly perf export at /dashboards/perf-summary.
Sam (Research): competitor snapshot: 1) Cloud providers: scale & reliability but opaque pricing. 2) Boutique inference vendors: aggressively low-cost but limited SLAs. 3) OSS runtimes: flexible but ops-heavy. we should highlight observability + safe fallbacks.
Darci (Strategy): messaging experiment: try two banners on the site next week: A) "Inference you can operate." B) "Predictable inference across cloud, private, and dedicated." measure signup & demo requests.
Maria (CEO): question for leadership: how public should the model performance grid be? full numbers per model or summarized tiers?
Lena (Head Product): propose tiers + vetted benchmarks for our verified models. allow BYOM but tag it "experimental: requires verification". produce short eval notes per verified model.
Tom (Sales): please produce a quick compare sheet for verified vs community checkpoints (latency/cost/notes) for demos. makes customer conversations smoother.
Priya (Eng): BYOM checklist items: quant support, max sequence length, memory profile, KV cache behavior. i'll write a draft and post in #eng.
Ajay (CTO): one more technical guardrail: avoid absolute promises like "X ms latency" without specifying load, seq, and batch. give ranges and the knob to improve them.
Sam (Research): model ecosystem moves fastwe should commit to a regular review cadence (quarterly) for the verified list. Darci, can strategy own that?
Darci (Strategy): yes, will set quarterly reviews and a simple rubric for additions/removals.
Maria (CEO): final: GTM packs. do we want separate collateral for PLG vs enterprise?
Tom (Sales): yesPLG: quickstarts and a simple API story. Enterprise: SLAs, private deploy, dedicated pricing, and compliance docs.
Lena (Head Product): also surface Redwood Optimize recommendations in both tracks; depth differs.
Priya (Eng): will share typical cost-savings ranges from Optimize once we have validated numbers.
Maria (CEO): great thread. i'll synthesize into a short comms README and two one-pagers (PLG + enterprise) later today. thanks all. :sparkles:
